=== v_value_independence ===
CREATE VIEW v_value_independence AS
    SELECT COALESCE(parameter_canonical, parameter) AS parameter,
           population_code,
           COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(root_ref_id, root_id)) AS independent_root_count
    FROM source_value_extractions
    WHERE root_type IN ('measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                        'derived_calculation')
      AND (root_ref_id IS NOT NULL
           OR root_id IN (SELECT root_id FROM external_root_registry))
    GROUP BY COALESCE(parameter_canonical, parameter), population_code

=== v_root_id_conflicts ===
CREATE VIEW v_root_id_conflicts AS
    SELECT 'ref_id_has_multiple_root_ids' AS conflict_type,
           root_ref_id AS conflict_key,
           COUNT(DISTINCT root_id) AS distinct_count
    FROM source_value_extractions
    WHERE root_ref_id IS NOT NULL AND root_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY root_ref_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT root_id) > 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'root_id_spans_multiple_ref_ids' AS conflict_type,
           root_id AS conflict_key,
           COUNT(DISTINCT root_ref_id) AS distinct_count
    FROM source_value_extractions
    WHERE root_ref_id IS NOT NULL AND root_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY root_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT root_ref_id) > 1

=== v_divergence ===
CREATE VIEW v_divergence AS
    SELECT ecs.*, ca.status AS convergence_status, ca.rationale AS convergence_rationale,
           ca.synthesis_approach AS convergence_synthesis_approach
    FROM "specifications" ecs
    JOIN convergence_assessment ca ON ca.convergence_id = ecs.convergence_id
    WHERE ca.status = 'divergent'

=== v_best_practice ===
CREATE VIEW v_best_practice AS
    SELECT *,
           CASE
               WHEN regulatory_stratum_only = 1 THEN 'weak'
               ELSE 'anchored'
           END AS strength_band
    FROM "specifications"
    WHERE state IN ('stated', 'provisional')
      AND code_floor_only = 0

=== v_pending ===
CREATE VIEW v_pending AS
    SELECT ecs.*, g.description AS gap_description, g.category AS gap_category,
           g.priority AS gap_priority
    FROM "specifications" ecs
    JOIN gaps g ON g.gap_id = ecs.gap_register_id
    WHERE ecs.state = 'pending'

=== v_source_admission ===
CREATE VIEW v_source_admission AS
SELECT
    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,
    es.evidence_type,
    es.verification_status,
    es.verification_disposition,
    se.exec_id,
    se.slug                     AS admitted_under_slug,
    se.query_text,
    se.engine,
    se.language,
    se.jurisdiction             AS search_jurisdiction,
    se.depth_method,
    se.mining_direction,
    se.target_tier,
    se.backfill                 AS search_was_backfilled,
    se.session                  AS admitting_session,
    se.executed_at              AS admitted_at,
    -- The research-stage prior, reached by pointer rather than copied onto the
    -- evidence row. This is what makes CHECK 7 answerable.
    se.prior_expectation
FROM evidence_sources es
JOIN search_admissions sa ON sa.ref_id  = es.ref_id
JOIN search_executions se ON se.exec_id = sa.exec_id

=== search_executions ===
CREATE TABLE search_executions (
  exec_id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  slug                 TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),
  jurisdiction         TEXT,                 -- NULL = jurisdiction-agnostic search
  language             TEXT NOT NULL,        -- ISO; one of the 19 research languages
  -- hierarchy branch the search TARGETED (diffable against what was FOUND):
  target_tier          INTEGER CHECK (target_tier IS NULL OR target_tier BETWEEN 1 AND 6),
  target_evidence_type TEXT CHECK (target_evidence_type IS NULL OR target_evidence_type IN
     ('clinical','sr_meta','standard_eb','national_fw','code','co1','co2','grey')),
  target_scope         TEXT CHECK (target_scope IS NULL OR target_scope IN
     ('intrinsic','lower_control','high_control','national','international')),
  -- the verbatim, replayable query:
  query_text           TEXT NOT NULL,
  terms_used           TEXT,                 -- JSON array of term ids
  engine               TEXT NOT NULL,        -- pubmed|crossref|scholar|biorxiv|medrxiv|consensus|web|registry|manual
  -- depth as real method, not booleans:
  depth_method         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (depth_method IN ('scoping','systematic')),
  mining_direction     TEXT CHECK (mining_direction IS NULL OR mining_direction IN
     ('none','backward','forward','both')),

# DR-2026-09-02-finish-the-render-sweep — Finish the render sweep: archive the site surfaces that publish the deleted item layer.

**Status:** **RATIFIED ON CONTACT** — this is an owner ruling, and `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 holds that
a live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches **on contact**. Owner
rulings do not await ratification; this record exists so the ruling is citable by the machine and
findable by a reader, not to confer validity it already has.

**Register row:** `D-0186` · category `D-OP` · delegation `DG-NON` ·
decided by `jordanelias` on 2026-09-02 19:15 · `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml`

> **This file is GENERATED from its register row.** Edit the register, not this file — two
> hand-maintained copies of one decision is the dual home rule 5 forbids, and C9 exists to catch
> exactly that drift.

## Outcome

ADOPTED by owner ruling 2026-09-02, choosing option B of two put to the owner.

## Rationale

The 2026-09-01 retraction deleted site/specs and stopped, leaving site/populations publishing 172 links across 79 item codes and both index pages pointing into a directory that no longer existed. No gate caught it because validate_cross_refs treats site/ as REFERENCE_ONLY. DR-2026-08-19 §1.2 had predicted exactly this: 'archiving the items rows quarantines none of this -- a researcher who greps the repository for their slug will meet the old answer before they have logged their first search.' Leaving the surface half-swept was the one disposition ruled out: neither frozen nor swept, just broken.

## Alternatives considered

- Treat site/ as a frozen reference surface and restore site/specs -- rejected by the owner: it keeps publishing determinations the data no longer holds.
- Leave the state as it was -- ruled out before the choice was put: half a rendered surface is not a disposition.

## Notes, and what remains owed

CORRECTS AN EARLIER SESSION ERROR. The 93 spec pages were deleted outright on 2026-09-01. CLAUDE.md §1 holds that git history is the archive for CODE and _archived/ is the right home for retired CONTENT; rendered pages are content. They are restored to _archived/site/specs/, which also makes the archived index.html's relative links resolve, and root index.html's six links are repointed there. UNEXPLAINED, STATED RATHER THAN TIDIED: two pages, [cross-cutting].html and [unassigned].html, arrived in the restore set. They are real rendered pages appearing nowhere in git history -- 93 were deleted and 93 existed at befaa29^. Kept because they are content, but the mechanism by which they entered the set was not reconstructed and no mechanism was invented. OWED: root index.html still states the determination 'Corridor Clear Width (>=1200 mm Minimum on All Primary Routes)' as fact on its front page. Rewriting the landing page's framing is mission-level content and was not done here.

## Delegation

Owner ruling. What the project publishes is work-product inclusion, DG-NON under governance/decision-protocol.md.

##### decisions/DR-2026-09-02-restore-research-code-leads.md
# DR-2026-09-02-restore-research-code-leads — Restore the 83 archived code/standard leads as research_code_leads, executing D-0181 rather than superseding it.

**Status:** **RATIFIED ON CONTACT** — this is an owner ruling, and `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 holds that
a live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches **on contact**. Owner
rulings do not await ratification; this record exists so the ruling is citable by the machine and
findable by a reader, not to confer validity it already has.

**Register row:** `D-0185` · category `D-OP` · delegation `DG-NON` ·
decided by `jordanelias` on 2026-09-02 19:10 · `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml`

> **This file is GENERATED from its register row.** Edit the register, not this file — two
> hand-maintained copies of one decision is the dual home rule 5 forbids, and C9 exists to catch
> exactly that drift.

## Outcome

ADOPTED by owner ruling 2026-09-02, choosing option A of three put to the owner.

## Rationale

The 2026-09-01 base-and-research-only ruling emptied jurisdictional_values as a side effect of deleting the item layer, because its item_code column is NOT NULL REFERENCES items. Neither quoted ruling named the table, and DR-2026-08-19 §1.5 had demanded the opposite sequencing: decide it separately, 'it must not be collateral damage'. It was collateral damage. D-0181 of 2026-08-31 had already called these rows research and already named the successor table, so restoring them EXECUTES that decision. Measured: the 109 archived records carry three non-null columns and collapse to 83 distinct (jurisdiction, standard_name) leads across 12 jurisdictions; the other 26 are the same standard restated per design parameter. 100% of surviving information is item-independent, so the only thing dropped is the item link -- the thing the ruling says must not exist -- and it survives in the archived filenames for provenance.

## Alternatives considered

- Confirm the deletion and record it as superseding D-0181 -- rejected by the owner: ~72 of the 83 leads exist nowhere else and would die with the archive.
- Merge them into source_locators -- rejected: that store already carries 24 rows holding both a standard_number and a DOI, and a standard has no DOI. That misalignment is what made REF-00037 carry a PLoS ONE DOI against a RIBA housing-guide title and falsely block an admission on 2026-09-01.

## Notes, and what remains owed

OWED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE. jurisdictional_values is left in place and empty rather than dropped, because v_code_floor_only reads it and CLAUDE.md holds a cross-stage view to be the most protected object in the schema -- the pointer rule 5's point-don't-copy actually means in SQL. That view joins on item_code, a column the owner ruled out of existence, so what it becomes is its own question. ALSO OWED: 11 of the 83 standards also appear in source_locators.standard_number and are reconciliation debt, not a licence to duplicate; and research_code_leads.jurisdiction carries NO CHECK because the vocabulary's nearest home, lang_jur_map, lacks two of the twelve values restored (GB and ISO, the latter a standards body rather than a country) -- registering a real jurisdiction vocabulary and pointing both at it is owed, not faked. D-0181's own note is now stale: it says the rename lands in 'the parked migration 065', but slot 065 was consumed by the four-lens link table on 2026-09-01.

## Delegation

Owner ruling. Work-product inclusion and the disposition of a retired corpus are judgements about the book, which governance/decision-protocol.md places in the DG-NON class and CLAUDE.md rule 0 makes non-delegable. DR-2026-08-19 §1.5 named this consequence specifically and demanded it be decided 'as its own decision, before items is touched'.

# DR-2026-09-02-strike-the-item-frame-pull — Strike DR-2026-08-19 §12.1 step 2's item-frame query; replace it with an ICF-first frame pull.

**Status:** **RATIFIED ON CONTACT** — this is an owner ruling, and `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 holds that
a live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches **on contact**. Owner
rulings do not await ratification; this record exists so the ruling is citable by the machine and

> hand-maintained copies of one decision is the dual home rule 5 forbids, and C9 exists to catch
> exactly that drift.

## Outcome

ADOPTED by owner ruling 2026-09-02.

## Rationale

The instrument contradicted itself at the point it was most trusted. §1.4 rule 1 says a slug is authored from the ICF/access-need frame first and the item list consulted for coverage 'never to supply one'; rule 2 says 'No value crosses' from an item name into a search_executions or search_candidates row. §12.1 step 2 ordered the frame pulled from items. A session obeying the runbook therefore broke the quarantine, and on 2026-09-01 one did: FRAME.md was derived from items and the item values '22 N' and 'PTV >=36' reached agonist queries. The step is also inert three times over -- items is empty, and item_axis_links and item_population_links were dropped by migration 065.

## Alternatives considered

- Amend §1.4 instead so the item frame becomes lawful -- rejected: §1.4 is the quarantine, and the measured harm ran the other way.
- Leave both and rely on sessions to notice -- rejected: one did not, which is why this exists.

## Notes, and what remains owed

Struck in place with the original text preserved, per the D-0181 precedent that editing a ratified DR's runbook is done under explicit owner ruling with the struck text kept in the record. THE REPLACEMENT STATES TWO GAPS RATHER THAN PAPERING OVER THEM, both created by the 2026-09-01 retraction and neither repaired: term_item_links was the only route from terms and term_aliases (88 and 2,382 rows) to a research subject and is now empty, so R11's terms_used has no slug route; and slugs.serves_axes is populated on 1 of 106 rows, so the cross-product the step pulls is generic rather than slug-specific. A runbook step that cannot execute is the defect this strike removes, so the step says only what is actually reachable.

## Delegation

Owner ruling amending a RATIFIED Decision Record. CLAUDE.md rule 0: a live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches, on contact.

summary: The lens is a COLUMN, not a traversal: one item×taxonomy link table with four nullable lens pointers. item_axis_links is folded in; base_taxonomy_medical is created.
outcome: ADOPTED and landed as migration 065. item_population_links (372) and item_axis_links (158) become item_taxonomy_links (530), carrying identity_code, icf_code, needs_code and medical_code. base_taxonomy_medical is created empty.
rationale: Executes D-0170's four lenses and D-0182's cardinality against the owner's stated goal of a dynamically rendering site with a multimodal lens and filters. The alternative -- store a fact in one lens and cross to the others at render through population_axis_map / access_need_axis_map -- was measured on 2026-09-01 and fails twice. (1) THE CROSSINGS ARE INCOMPLETE: identity→ICF 20 of 23, ICF→identity 16 of 17, needs→ICF 15 of 17, ICF→needs 15 of 17, and identity↔needs has no direct map at all; every gap is a silently empty page rather than a "no results" page. (2) TRAVERSAL MANUFACTURES INFERENCE AND CHANGES THE ANSWER: the identity lens asked for DEAF returns 20 items, while the ICF lens asked for AX-AUD -- the axis DEAF crosses to -- returns 38 rows, because DEAFBLIND crosses to AX-AUD too. Only the first is a recorded fact. D-0174 reserves applicability to synthesis, so a render layer that crosses is adjudicating where nothing reviews it and no attestation covers it. With the lens as a column the render is WHERE <lens>_code = ?, one query shape for four lenses, and no UNION anywhere -- a UNION is only forced when the taxonomies live in separate link tables, which is the state this ends.

the workings: every tool call, every query, every intermediate result, verbatim.

## Why it exists

On 2026-09-02 the owner asked whether the adversarial pass's direct workings had been
lost. They had been about to be. The antagonist ran read-only and wrote nothing itself;
its findings reached the repository only through commit messages and a defect register,
and the `antagonist/` scratchpad directory stood empty. Its transcript existed **only in
ephemeral container storage** and would have gone when the container was reclaimed.

That had already happened once in the same session: the first antagonist run was killed
mid-flight by a container restart, and everything it had done survived only because the
orchestrator happened to have read its partial output before it died.

**The project's infrastructure is incomplete, so the transcripts are how we audit the
workflow itself.** A conclusion you cannot trace is a conclusion you cannot correct.

## What is here

`harness_<id>/main.jsonl` — the orchestrator's own transcript for that harness session.
`harness_<id>/subagents/<started>_<role>_<agentid>.jsonl` — one per subagent.
`harness_<id>/index.json` — machine-readable: start time, role, size, agent id, filename.

Roles are **derived from each agent's own brief**, not from filenames. Note that
`ANTAGONIST` contains the substring `AGONIST`; a naive match mislabels every antagonist
as an agonist, which it did once here before being caught.

# session_2026-09-02-research-batch-05-circulation-icf

**Research batch 05 · slug `accessible-circulation-geometry` · ICF-first frame · three agents**

Volatile figures below were derived from `data/guidebook.db` and
`retrieval-log/session_2026-09-02-research-batch-05-circulation-icf/manifest.jsonl`
after the migration applied, not carried from the working conversation.

---

## What this batch was for

Three jobs at once, at the owner's direction: **perform research**, **ensure compliance
with process**, **log the work**. Run as three agents — an **agonist** that retrieves and
vets before anything is written, an **antagonist** that attacks the filed rows, and a
**tracer** that records actions, errors, gaps and failures for audit.

The frame was pulled ICF-first for the first time, under D-0187: axes with codes AND
names, access needs, populations and their crossing maps. No item codes and no item
values entered the frame, and it declared its own two gaps (`slugs.serves_axes`
populated on 1 of 106 rows; no term↔slug link exists, so R11's `terms_used` cannot be
populated from the slug) rather than reading a generic frame as a scoped one.

## What landed

| | |
|---|---|
| `evidence_sources` | 9, one of them Co-1 |
| searches logged | 15, of which 5 carry a harm finding |
| candidates staged | 15 |
| population matches | 14, including one dissenting second row |
| citation-mining rows | 5 this batch, 15 in the table |
| leads promoted | 1 (the first `PROMOTED` in 881 locator rows) |
| payloads retained | 49, 4,626,254 bytes, one of them a PDF |
| schema | `user_version` 67, unchanged |

`research_batch_dod.py`: **COMPLIANT, 17/17**. `retrieval_log --verify-authors`:
**CLEAN on 8 examined**. `migrate_db.py --rebuild`: reproducible. All DB-derived outputs
regenerated and `--check`-clean.

## The findings that were worth the batch

**Circulation geometry is the most-cited in-building barrier disabled people report.**
Euan's Guide Access Survey 2025 (REF-00978, Co-1, over 4,400 respondents, 88% of them
disabled people), question 7, p.13–14: *"I could not get around the venue (e.g. lack of
lifts, narrow corridors, too little space or poor layout)"* — **56%**, against *"could
not get into the venue"* 41% and *"no access to a toilet that suits my requirements"*
41%. Second of twelve options overall, behind parking at 64%.

**The shoulder-load penalty is incurred by the existence of a slope, not by its
steepness.** Marchiori, Gagnon & Pradon 2023 (REF-00973), Table 3: shoulder
flexion/extension push-phase HIGH risk runs 12.2% level → 44.5% → 47.0% → 45.2% across
1:20, 1:16, 1:12. The authors' own reading: *"greater efforts are required to propulse
the wheelchair from the smallest slope (2.7°), but that this effort does not increase
further with the increasing slope."* A frame built from an item called "Ramp Gradient
(≤1:20)" would have gone looking for the difference between 1:20 and 1:12 and found the
wrong question.

**A published error, flagged.** That same paper's §2.2 says *"The four slopes greater
than 0° corresponded to slopes that increase from one unit of height to 20, 16, 12 and 8
units of length"* — four ratios for three slopes. arctan settles the mapping:
2.86°/3.58°/4.76° ⇒ 1:20/1:16/1:12. **1:8 is 7.13° and was never tested.** Anyone citing
this paper for a 1:8 result cites its error.

**Ramp *descent* outranks fast propulsion for shoulder load**, and the discourse is all
about ascent (REF-00974, abstract-level locator, ten able-bodied participants — the
ordering is the claim, not the newtons).

**A 49-record Japanese J-STAGE seam invisible to English engines**, including 2003 prior
art (REF-00976, admitted under R5: non-English peer-reviewed work is academic, and
non-indexation is an indexing fact).

## What went wrong, and was caught

**Three fabricated bibliographic fields were filed and passed every gate.** REF-00976
stored a title no payload asserts and a co-author given name three payloads contradict
(*Naoji* → *Toshiyuki*); REF-00973 stored a title bent toward the slug it was admitted
for. `--verify-authors` printed CLEAN over all three, because it compared **family names
only** and never looked at given names or at titles at all — CLAUDE.md §2(a) at field
granularity, inside the module written to prevent §2(c). It also indexed only Crossref's
single-work envelope, so three of eight sources reported as *"NO LOGGED RETRIEVAL — not
verifiable offline"* over payloads sitting on disk. `EXAMINED` went 5 → 8 on the same log
once fixed.

**The one disability-led source was screened out on a 404.** exec 34 logged a
*"Page not found"* page — 15,580 bytes containing no occurrence of *survey*,
*respondent*, *toilet* or *staff* — and then characterised the report's content from it,
as *"predominantly information provision, toilets and staff attitude rather than
circulation geometry"*, with *"6000+ respondents in 2023"* beside it. That sentence was
the reason nothing was admitted. R10 says a block is not a terminal answer and a 404 is
not either: the live report was one hop from the homepage, and its most-cited in-building
barrier is the slug's own subject. That the guess was directionally plausible about
toilets is luck, not method.

**A systematic review was about to be counted as convergence with two of its own included
studies.** REF-00977 (Kapsalis 2022) contains REF-00971 (Dutta part I) and REF-00784
(Koontz — the batch's declared anchor) among its 48 included studies. Established from
the review's own logged Crossref record: keys `e_1_3_3_43_1`–`e_1_3_3_90_1` are exactly
48 entries in first-author alphabetical order, bounded by the methods citations below and
by the restart of ordering above. **Those DOIs were in this batch's own `citation_mining`
row from 21:11.** The list was stored and never read back, and only an adversarial reader
caught it.

**My own errors, in order of seriousness.** (1) `REF-00978.co1_provenance` — the field
carrying the CRPD Art 4.3 warrant — ended *"verified from the retrieved report itself
(p.2, p.28), not from a description of it"*. p.2 is blank but for the running header,
p.28 is survey question 40, and the charity registration number the sentence carried
appears nowhere in the 29 pages: it came from the web description the sentence denied. A
verification assertion that is itself the thing that failed. (2) I recorded circulation
as *"the single most-cited barrier in the survey"* having read the two options beside
each other rather than all twelve; parking at 64% outranks it. Corrected on all three
affected rows and in the commit message, which had not been pushed. (3) A
population-match note claimed self-selection *"does not affect the RANKING of barriers"*
— unevidenced, and most likely wrong in a specific direction, since the survey is
supported by the Motability Scheme, 91% of respondents own or lease a car, and the
top-ranked barrier is parking.

AFTER_DATA_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^--\s*AFTER_DATA:\s*(\d{14})\s*$", re.M)


def build_plan() -> list:
    """The faithful replay order, as a flat list of steps.

    Returns [("schema", version, path), ("data", ts, migration_id, path), ...].

    THE DEFAULT is what it has always been: every schema migration, then every
    data migration. That is right almost always, because schema precedes the
    data it shapes.

    IT IS WRONG WHENEVER A SCHEMA MIGRATION RENAMES OR DROPS SOMETHING THAT
    COMMITTED DATA MIGRATIONS STILL NAME. Data migrations are immutable, so they
    keep writing to the old name forever; a schema-phase rename runs first and
    they die on replay. Migration 025 hit this from the other side and had to
    withdraw a data migration to escape it. The 055 rename hit it from this side
    across 19 data migrations spanning two months, where withdrawal is not
    available.

    A numbered schema migration may therefore declare, on its own line:

        -- AFTER_DATA: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS

    meaning: this migration, and every migration numbered after it, applies only
    once the data migrations up to that timestamp have replayed. That is not a
    special case bolted on for one rename — it is the real chronology, which the
    numbered/timestamped split cannot otherwise express. Several markers may be
    present; each opens another data segment.
    """
    schema_migs = discover_schema_migrations()
    data_migs = discover_data_migrations()
    marks = []
    for i, (_v, path) in enumerate(schema_migs):
        m = AFTER_DATA_PATTERN.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if m:
            marks.append((i, m.group(1)))

    plan, si, di = [], 0, 0
    for idx, cutoff in marks:
        plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:idx]]
        si = idx
        while di < len(data_migs) and data_migs[di][0] <= cutoff:
            plan.append(("data",) + data_migs[di])
            di += 1
    plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:]]
    plan += [("data",) + d for d in data_migs[di:]]
    return plan


def _apply_one_data_migration(conn, migration_id, path, applied_by_session):

    Body and ledger row now commit as one unit -- see _apply_atomically.
    """

content.content:
# `e150` is not a lens, and the reason it isn't is doctrinal

Owner, 2026-09-01: *"e150 is building design. there are no users who use this guidebook who have
the code 'e150' apply to themselves."* · *"it does raise the point that e150 and universal design
etc etc etc all touch on the idea of utopian/idealized building design for mode population all"*

## The correction, first

I framed the 38 `e`-typed rows in `access_need_icf` as *"this project's ICF usage is overwhelmingly
environmental"* and concluded that adopting the 44 WHO domains *"would delete the environmental
dimension."* **That treats `e` codes as lens data being lost. They were never lens data.**

A lens is **how a reader identifies themselves**. `e` codes are Environmental Factors — they
describe the world. Nobody *is* an `e150`. So:

- **The 44 are right for the ICF lens, with no caveat.** The lens is person-side and `b`/`d` are the
  person-side ICF chapters. The owner's ruling stands unqualified; my caveat was misframed.
- **My "fifth lens" and "`environment_code` column on the link table" options were a category
  error** — they would have put world-facts in a table of person-facts.

## The distinction that was missing

**A lens is who the reader IS. A filter is what the reader is LOOKING FOR.**

The stated goal carries both: *"presented according to which lens the user chooses and what filters
they have selected."* `e` codes are filter vocabulary, never lens vocabulary. Getting that
backwards is what produced the wrong recommendation.

## But the filter vocabulary already exists, and it is better

`items.category`, A–K, measured against the live items:

| | domain | items |
|---|---|---|
| A | acoustics | 19 |
| B | lighting | 12 |
| C | colour, pattern, finish | 6 |
| D | plan and wayfinding | 11 |
| E | circulation and vertical movement | 14 |
| F | sensory gradient and olfactory | 8 |
| G | furniture, seating, grab bars | 9 |
| H | controls and information systems | 5 |
| I | hardware and fittings | 4 |
| K | DeafBlind, tactile, intervenor | 5 |
| J | *declared in the CHECK, zero items* | 0 |

This is **more specific than ICF `e`, not less.** `A-18 RT60 in Occupied Learning and Listening
Spaces` is `e250 Sound` made specific. `E-08 Corridor Clear Width` is `e150 building design
(public)` made specific. Adding the `e` codes on top would be a **second home for a fact
`items.category` already states** — rule 5.

## And the owner's second point is why it would be worse than redundant

`e150 building design (public)` and *universal design* both name **a building designed well for
everyone** — a modal subject. This project's own data already rejects that frame, in its own words.
`populations.description` for `BAR`:

> *"Body-size group; frame as the environment wrongly normed to an average body."*

**The defect is in the norm, not in the person.** That is the guidebook's doctrine, written down,
about the exact thing `e150` presupposes. Importing `e150` as vocabulary would import the
presupposition the project exists to interrogate.

## `ALL` is that presupposition already inside the identity lens

Measured 2026-09-01 against the live database:

| | |
|---|---|
| identity-lens rows | 382 |
| carrying `identity_code = 'ALL'` | **9** (2.4%), across **9 items of 93** |
| of those, carrying a `rationale_ref` | **0** |
| written by | 8 from `session_2026-05-11-items-population-normalization`, 1 from `session_2026-07-13-contradiction-sweep-f07-recovery` |

And `populations.description` for `ALL` reads:

> *"Item is not population-specific; applies to everyone"*

That is the utopian claim, unwarranted, sitting in the data. Nine assertions that something applies
to everyone, none of them examined, all from normalisation passes rather than synthesis. Under
`D-0175` (OD-A) every one is a use-time debt nobody has paid, and under the full-cross-product
ruling (`DR-2026-08-24` §2.4) applicability is an **output** of synthesis, never an input — which
is exactly what a blanket `ALL` asserts as an input.

`ALL` also sits in `populations.category = 'general'` beside `BAR`, `LPA` and `TALL`, which are
three real identities. A scope marker bundled with three constituencies is its own defect.

**This is DG-NON and it is the owner's.** The options are: retire `ALL` and require the nine items
to name their populations; keep it but move it out of `populations` into something that is honestly
a scope marker rather than a population; or keep it and require a `rationale_ref` on every use, so
"applies to everyone" becomes a claim someone made rather than a default.

## A real drift found on the way

`schemas/item.py` declares **`category_name: str`** as a required field — its own comment says
`"Circulation" etc.` — and the `items` table has **no `category_name` column**. So the design-domain
vocabulary A–K has names **in the Pydantic model and nowhere in the database**. `CLAUDE.md` §7:
*"`schemas/*.py` ↔ SQLite drift is a bug, not a convention."*

Which means the recommendation is not "add ICF `e` codes to items" but its opposite:

> **Name A–K in the database.** The filter vocabulary this project needs already exists, is already
> specific to the built environment, and is already scoped to what the guidebook covers. What it
> lacks is names — and `J`, declared with zero items, needs either a meaning or removal from the
> CHECK.

## Net effect on what was owed

| previously owed | now |
|---|---|
| decide where `e` codes live (items / fifth column / one ICF vocabulary) | **withdrawn** — they live nowhere; `items.category` already does the work |
| the 44 replace the coined axes, with an environmental caveat | **caveat withdrawn**; the replacement is clean |
| `access_need_icf`'s 5 person-side rows re-point at the 44 | unchanged — and 3 of the 5 map exactly (`d510`→`VW20`, `d540`→`VW23`, `d550`→`VW24`) |
| — | **new:** `access_need_icf`'s 38 `e` rows are need→design-domain knowledge; re-express them against `items.category`, not against ICF |

# Owner rulings — 2026-09-01, during research batch 04

Recorded at contact under CLAUDE.md rule 0: *"A live owner statement supersedes every prior
ratified record it touches, on contact. Your job on hearing one is to record the supersession,
never to weigh the ruling against the paperwork it changes."*

These are transcribed from the owner in session. They are not proposals and were not negotiated.

---

## R-01 — The item layer must not exist

> *"E-03, I-01, E-08 etc: WHY ARE THESE ALREADY EXISTING. THIS IS CONTAMINATION. I HAVE RULED SO
> MANY TIMES THAT THIS CANNOT ALREADY EXIST"*

**Reason, in the owner's own words:**

> *"IF WE ALREADY HAVE E-08 ETC, THEN ALL OF YOUR WORK IS PREDISPOSED TO FILING IT INTO A PLACE
> THAT ALREADY EXISTS WHICH IS A MAJOR BIAS AND LIMITING FACTOR FOR WORK BEING PERFORMED"*

**Disposition:** delete from the database. Confirmed by the owner when asked how to handle the
cascade.

**What this supersedes.** `DR-2026-08-19` §1 demoted the 93 items to "leads, not research topics"
and wrote a quarantine protocol at §1.4. Measured 2026-09-01: **all 93 items are `status='active'`
and `slugs.status='PROVISIONAL'` holds zero rows.** The quarantine was written and never executed.
A rhetorical demotion left the containers standing, which is the state in which the next session
files into them. It did.

**Scope, measured.** 93 items plus item-keyed dependents: `item_taxonomy_links` 540,
`term_item_links` 147, `jurisdictional_values` 109.

---

## R-02 — Nothing may be populated downstream of research

> *"THERE SHOULD BE ABSOLUTELY NO DATA POPULATED IN ROWS AFTER THE RESEARCH PHASE RIGHT NOW"*

**Measured state at the time of the ruling:** evidence 67 rows (`evidence_sources` 10,
`evidence_source_authors` 37, `source_slug_links` 10, `search_admissions` 10); judgment 25
(`evidence_population_match`). Synthesis, specification and render were already at zero.

**Owner confirmation on the prior batches:** yes, empty everything after research — this retracts
batches 01, 02 and 03.

**Owner confirmation on judgment specifically:**

> *"evidence_population_match 25 seems like it should be emptied/deleted for now"*

**Corroboration the project already held.** All ten admitted sources carry an open P1 gap saying
their content was never verified. `GAP-B01-001`: batch 1's five admissions had fabricated author
lists, *"12 of 19 author rows named non-authors."* `GAP-B02-001`: batch 2's five were admitted on
metadata alone, *"No full text was read."*

---

## R-03 — The database holds base and research, and nothing else

> *"we have our base, which includes all these clues and slugs from our prior work that we are
> deliberately retaining in a pared format where item codes etc should not exist with them, and we
> have our research. that's it. nothing else right now."*

**Pared** is the operative word: the clues and slugs are retained, and item codes are removed from
them.

---

## R-04 — DOI leads belong to research, not evidence

> *"the DOI lead lists were supposed to be in research or base"*
> *"DOI leads are not evidence because they aren't tied to anything. they're for research"*

**Consequence applied.** `citation_mining` (10 rows, 147 harvested DOI leads) is retained in
research with its `global_ref_id` foreign key set NULL, rather than deleted along with the evidence
it pointed at. `source_locators` (875 rows, the clue store) is untouched. A lead tied to nothing is
the definition of a clue, and a clue is research input.

---

## R-05 — Table names should carry their pipeline stage

> *"the nomenclature is difficult for me because the names of these tables aren't prepended by
> their assigned stage in pipeline"*

**Status: recorded, not yet executed.** This is a rename, and CLAUDE.md rule 4 makes a rename real
work — a view is a caller, and so is a skill; migration 064 exists because migration 063 swept eight
Python readers and six skills and missed `v_item_provenance`. The defect the ruling names is real
and measurable: nothing in `sqlite_master` says which stage a table belongs to, which is why
CLAUDE.md must instruct sessions to *derive* the table-to-stage assignment rather than read one.

**Sequencing recommendation, for the owner to accept or reject:** land the retraction first, then
sweep names against a schema that is mostly empty. Renaming tables that still carry dependent rows
is the more dangerous order.

---

`scripts/emit_data_migration.py --input ...` — the only sanctioned path for changing the database —
was denied by the harness permission classifier. The retraction migration is written and was

It cannot be applied until that command is approved. No workaround was attempted: hand-writing SQL
against `data/guidebook.db` is forbidden by CLAUDE.md rule 3.

# Agonist recommendation — the determination's subject, and the prior-version corpus

Read-only pass, measured against `origin/main` at `5572b6f` on 2026-09-09. Nothing was written. Every figure below either carries the command that produces it or is dated.

Two corrections to the brief before anything else, because both change the framing:

1. **`.ignore` does hide `versions/`.** Verified two ways: `rg -l 'Corridor Clear Width'` walked from the repo root returns no `versions/` path, and the Grep tool returns none either (`rg --debug` shows the root `.ignore` glob firing). My first test passed `versions/` as an explicit argument, which ripgrep never ignores, and that confounded it. So the unhidden surfaces are `references/`, `working/` and `index.html`; `versions/` is hidden from search and still fully readable. CLAUDE.md §7's item-layer bullet ("none of which `.ignore` hides") is wrong on that point and contradicts the bullet directly above it.
2. **The `[A-E]` regex in CLAUDE.md §7 is a floor, not the sweep.** Item categories run A–K. Measured 2026-09-09: `grep -rEl '\b[A-E]-[0-9]{2}\b' references/ versions/ working/ index.html | wc -l` → 201; with `[A-K]` → 235; repo-wide with `[A-K]`, excluding `.git/`, `_archived/`, `scratchpad/`, `transcripts/`, `sessions/`, `audits/`, `scripts/migrations/` → 403.

---

## ITEM 1 — What replaces `item_code` as the determination's subject

### 1. Recommendation

**This question is not open: the owner ruled on 2026-08-26 that the determination is keyed on the canonical design parameter, and on 2026-08-27 (D-0171) that `items` conflated element, parameter and determination "with no element table and no parameter registry to hold them apart" — nobody swept either; the sweep should realise the parameter as a judgment-minted registry whose name is a pointer into `terms`, whose existence is provable only from an admitted source's extraction (`minted_from_extraction_id NOT NULL`), keyed as `specifications.parameter_id NOT NULL`, at the grain parameter × lens-tuple (× room context), with the slug reached by pointer through the judgment chain rather than carried.**

### 2. Derivation

**The rulings, in order, none of them swept into schema.**

- **2026-08-25** (ledger `/home/user/guidebook/references/project-standards.md`, `grep -n 'A specification keys from the judgment object'`): *"specifications as a synthesis should be keying from a judgment item (if we use the word item) and cross-referencing itself against disability populations, access needs and ICF, ie all three modes."* Identity = judgment object; lenses = cross-reference. Left open: what the judgment object is called.
- **2026-08-26** (`grep -n 'The judgment object is the'` in the same file): owner selected, from options put, *"key on the canonical parameter."* Verbatim consequences recorded: *"`specifications.item_code`, presently NOT NULL, is dropped alongside `population_code`"*; *"reusing `source_value_extractions.parameter_canonical`"*; and the counter-consideration the ruling itself flagged — *"`parameter_canonical` has no CHECK, no registry table, and no writer… A key needs a vocabulary."* ACTION (2): *"A canonical-parameter vocabulary lands in or before that migration."*
- **2026-08-27, D-0171** (`/home/user/guidebook/decisions/DR-2026-08-27-base-building-three-levels-items-is-not-one.md:26-30`): *"items conflates the element (door), the parameter (STC) and the determination (>=35), with no element table and no parameter registry to hold them apart."* Three objects named: element (`base_elements`, unbuilt), parameter (registry, unbuilt), determination (`specifications`).
- **2026-08-27, hand-off ruling** (ledger ~L1486): the judgment item is the extraction — *"`source_value_extractions` is a JUDGMENT table"*; fan-out research→evidence→judgment, fan-in judgment→synthesis→specification through junctions; ACTION (4): *"`items` is retired as a table name outright — the word was the ambiguity."*
- **2026-09-01, R-01/R-03** (`/home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/pr-126-research-batch-04-accessible-circulation/RULINGS.md`, commit `befaa29`): the layer is deleted because *"if we already have E-08 etc, then all of your work is predisposed to filing it into a place that already exists."* This does not overturn 08-26; it executes its "items retired" half and removes the one clause 08-26 had kept (`items` surviving as a Part-4 render rollup — now render's derivation, consistent with "`render_items` is files, not rows").
- **2026-09-09, owner, this session** (`transcripts/harness_292c6e38/main.jsonl`): *"my issue with item code is that you kept contaminating it with items that were created in a prior version when we want to start fresh."* The objection is to the write direction and provenance of the container, not to there being a subject.

So `CLAUDE.md` §6 and the `db.py add-item` refusal text (`/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py:1872-1876`, *"an OPEN OWNER DECISION… do not invent one"*) are half right: it is the owner's, and the owner already decided. That sentence is the exact inverse failure the 2026-09-09 ledger entry names — *"declaring open a question already answered."*

**The subject already exists in embryo, and the judgment stage was always keyed on it.** `source_value_extractions.parameter TEXT NOT NULL` (verbatim, "e.g. RT60, door clear width") and `parameter_canonical` nullable ("normalized for join", `/home/user/guidebook/schemas/source_value_extraction.py:89`); `idx_sve_slug_param ON (slug, parameter_canonical)`; and `v_value_independence` — the input to `convergence_assessment` — groups by `COALESCE(parameter_canonical, parameter), population_code` with no `item_code` anywhere in it. Only `specifications` ever disagreed. Today: 0 rows, no writer (`grep -c source_value_extractions scripts/db.py` → 0), `item_code` on it is nullable and inert.

**Grain — per parameter, not per slug × parameter.** (a) The 08-26 key is the parameter alone. (b) `v_value_independence` carries no slug. (c) The 08-27 ruling diagnoses the pipeline's non-walkability as *"each stage is joined to the next through a shared topic label, not through the thing the previous stage produced"* — a slug key is that defect restated. (d) Slugs are pre-authored containers: 106 rows, of which 27 fed 87 of the 93 items (DR-2026-08-19 §1.1); keying on them is the owner's objection in a different column. (e) The fan-in means one specification may draw on syntheses from several slugs. The slug is reached by pointer: specification → syntheses → extractions → `slug`. The lens dimension is the ruled half (four columns, at least one, multiplicity fine), so the unique identity is parameter × lens-tuple, exactly the shape `idx_itl_row_identity` already uses.

**Why the name is a pointer into `terms`, not a label column (rule 5).** `terms` (88 rows) was deliberately retained on 2026-09-01 (R-03: "pared"), is grown with warrant by D-0173, and already holds value-free design parameters: TERM-001 `ramp gradient`, TERM-002 `corridor width` (scope note: "Dimensional parameter"), TERM-005 `operating force`, TERM-007 `reverberation time`, TERM-021 `door width` — with 2,382 multilingual aliases behind them, which batch 05 already searched with (`terms_used` `["TERM-002","TERM-021"]`). Measured 2026-09-09: zero `terms.canonical_en` values contain a digit or comparator (Python regex `[0-9≥≤<>=]|\b(min|max|minimum|maximum)\b` over the table → `[]`). A registry with its own `label = 'corridor width'` writes that fact in a second home. Pointing at `term_id` also answers the homonym objection for free: the element noun is already in the term (corridor width ≠ door width).

**What stops re-accretion into a presupposed list — the difference from `items` is the direction of write, mechanised:**
1. `judgment_parameters.minted_from_extraction_id NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions` → `source_value_extractions.ref_id NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources`. A parameter cannot exist before an admitted source stated a value for it. `items` were written months before research.
2. No writer takes a label. The only route in is `db.py adjudicate-parameter --extraction-id N`, mirroring `term_adjudications` (NAMES-EXISTING / NAMES-NEW / rationale NOT NULL). The registry is created EMPTY, as `base_taxonomy_medical` was; no seed migration; `_archived/` names are not an input (`research_code_leads.notes` already records "that link is deliberately NOT carried").
3. Labels cannot state their answer: the value-free property lives on `terms`, verified today, and the pipeline-contract criterion `base-parameter-vocabulary` ("its labels do not themselves assert determinations") is repointed from `validate_items.py` to `terms`/`judgment_parameters`, printing `EXAMINED`.
4. Research never reads it. D-0187's ICF-first frame pull draws on axes, access needs, populations and crossing maps; `judgment_parameters` is not added to that pull.

### 3. Concrete shape

```sql
-- Judgment-stage satellite (the hand-off object judgment_items IS source_value_extractions, ruled 2026-08-27).
CREATE TABLE judgment_parameters (
  parameter_id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  term_id                    TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),          -- the name, by pointer
  minted_from_extraction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
  rationale                  TEXT    NOT NULL,
  status                     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                             CHECK (status IN ('active','merged','retired')),
  merged_into                INTEGER REFERENCES judgment_parameters(parameter_id),
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL, created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT,          updated_by_session TEXT
);
-- element_code REFERENCES base_elements(...) is ADDED (NULL-forward) when base_elements lands (ruled 2026-08-27, unbuilt).
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_jp_term ON judgment_parameters(term_id) WHERE status='active';

-- The D-0173 shape, verbatim, one stage on: the extraction's verbatim `parameter` is the observed
-- surface form; this row is the adjudication. No UNIQUE on extraction_id: a dissent is a second row
-- (same reasoning as add-population-match, CLAUDE.md §4).
CREATE TABLE parameter_adjudications (
  adjudication_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  extraction_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
  outcome          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN
                     ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW','NOT-A-PARAMETER','DEFERRED')),
  parameter_id     INTEGER REFERENCES judgment_parameters(parameter_id),
  rationale        TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL, created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,
  CHECK ((outcome IN ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW') AND parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
      OR (outcome IN ('NOT-A-PARAMETER','DEFERRED')  AND parameter_id IS NULL))
);

-- specifications: drop-and-recreate is legal today — 0 rows and NO INSERT in any migration, schema or data
-- (grep -lE 'INSERT INTO "?specifications"? ' scripts/migrations/*.sql → none, re-measured 2026-09-09).
CREATE TABLE specifications (
  specification_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  parameter_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES judgment_parameters(parameter_id),   -- THE SUBJECT
  -- the lens half, as ruled 2026-08-28 / D-0182 — not this item's question, but the sweep is owed here
  identity_code     TEXT REFERENCES populations(population_code),
  icf_code          TEXT REFERENCES axes(axis_code),
  needs_code        TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
  medical_code      TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),
  room_code         TEXT REFERENCES rooms(room_code),   -- context cross-reference; CHOICE POINT, see §6
  -- every other existing column carried verbatim: state, design_scale, convergence_id, confidence_*,
  -- gap_register_id, not_applicable_rationale, tier_basis, governing_refs, rule_version, derivation_sha,
  -- code_floor_only, value_min/max/unit, falsification_condition, has_unverified_sources,
  -- all_sources_disqualified, regulatory_stratum_only, the four stamps
  CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_spec_row_identity ON specifications(
  parameter_id, COALESCE(identity_code,''), COALESCE(icf_code,''),
  COALESCE(needs_code,''), COALESCE(medical_code,''), COALESCE(room_code,''));
```

`source_value_extractions`: ADD COLUMN `parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES judgment_parameters(parameter_id)` (NULL = not yet adjudicated). `item_code` stays, nullable, writer-retired, NULL forward — SQLite refuses `DROP COLUMN` on a column in a FOREIGN KEY constraint, and the 08-27 ruling says do not redesign this table. `parameter_canonical`: writer-retire, NULL forward; the 08-26 ACTION (3) "add-extraction must require `parameter_canonical`" becomes "add-extraction requires `parameter` verbatim; adjudication fills `parameter_id`."

**Every table carrying `item_code`, and its treatment** (derived with the CLAUDE.md §4 unwritable-column script plus `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`; all 0 rows):

| column | NOT NULL | committed INSERTs | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `specifications.item_code` | yes | none | recreate as above |
| `item_taxonomy_links.item_code` | yes | **`data_20260901183203`** (540 rows, since deleted) | cannot be altered in the schema phase — replay would die on that INSERT. Create `parameter_taxonomy_links` fresh with `parameter_id` in place of `item_code`, every other column and the four lens FKs verbatim, `idx_*_row_identity` mirrored; leave `item_taxonomy_links` dead-empty; drop later under `-- AFTER_DATA: 20260901205639` (the directive exists: `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/migrate_db.py:282-330`; `057` already uses it) |
| `source_value_extractions.item_code` | no | none | NULL forward; add `parameter_id` |
| `spec_value_probes.item_code` | yes | none | rebuild keyed on `parameter_id NOT NULL`; `v_pmp_latest_walk` regroups |
| `conflicts.item_code` | no | none | ADD `parameter_id`, NULL-forward `item_code` |
| `item_population_elaborations` | yes | none | delete (§8): it is the retired `population_code` shape; per-lens rows on `specifications` replace it |
| `item_audit_runs` | yes | none | delete: its pipeline was culled 2026-08-20 (`git log --diff-filter=D -- scripts/item_audit_pipeline.py` → `80a34d1`) |
| `item_bpc_links` | yes | none | delete: 08-27 finding, "named for BPC and does not reference `bpc_metadata`" |
| `term_item_links` | yes | baseline 057 (147, deleted) | leave dead; term↔parameter is now `judgment_parameters.term_id`; the owed term↔slug route (D-0187) is research's, not this |
| `jurisdictional_values` | yes | baseline 057 (109, deleted) | leave, per D-0185 (owner question because `v_code_floor_only` reads it); re-derive that view over `source_value_extractions WHERE jurisdiction IS NOT NULL` joined on `parameter_id` |
| `room_items` | yes | none | building layer: re-point to `base_elements` when it lands (ruled 08-27); not this subject |
| `case_study_specs`, `economics_entry_specs` | yes | none | their parents are also unwritable; re-key only if the parent tables are being redesigned in the same change, otherwise leave dead |
| `items` | — | baseline 057 (93, deleted) | leave; `DROP TABLE` only in a later migration under `AFTER_DATA` |

**Views (a view is a caller — the 064 lesson):** `v_item_extractions`, `v_item_provenance`, `v_source_reach_all`, `v_code_floor_only`, `v_pmp_latest_walk` re-derived on `parameter_id JOIN terms` for the name; `v_value_independence` regrouped by `parameter_id` and lens (08-26 ACTION 4). No triggers reference `item_code` (checked `sqlite_master`).

**Callers to sweep, derived not listed:** `grep -rl item_code scripts/*.py scripts/audit/*.py scripts/research/*.py tools/*.py schemas/*.py | wc -l` → 21 today; `grep -rl item_code skills/*.md | wc -l` → 12. Named because they will be missed otherwise: `/home/user/guidebook/tools/pipeline_completeness.py:153-240` (five queries on `items`/`item_code`), `/home/user/guidebook/schemas/specification.py` (SPEC-NNNN and `item_code` validators), `/home/user/guidebook/schemas/item.py` (model of a dead table), `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` criterion `base-parameter-vocabulary`, `governance/check-registry.yaml` entry `validate_items`, and the two prose callers that assert the question is open: `CLAUDE.md` §6 and `scripts/db.py:1872-1876`.

**Writers ship with the migration** (walkability §9.7-C; CLAUDE.md §4: a keyed table with no refusing writer is the hand-SQL gap): `add-extraction` (owed since 08-26), `adjudicate-parameter`, `add-specification` — respecting the 2026-08-25 ACTION (2) that `--state stated` is not built (see §6, gap).

**Migration mechanics:** one schema migration `071_*`, `user_version` 70 → 71; no `AFTER_DATA` needed for anything above because nothing is dropped that a data migration names; verify with `migrate_db.py --rebuild` and `scripts/audit/rename_insurance.py` as 065 did; mirror the Pydantic models; the ledger entry and a register row citing 08-25, 08-26, D-0171 as the authority; correct `CLAUDE.md` §6 and the `add-item` refusal to cite the ruling rather than call it open.

### 4. Alternatives rejected, and the strongest case against

- **`slug × lens`** — ruled out by the brief and by the derivation: slug is a research-stage label, pre-authored, and joining stages by topic label is the diagnosed non-walkability.
- **Bare `specifications.term_id` with no registry** (zero new tables). Genuinely tempting under §8. Rejected because a term can be minted by NAMES-NEW from a harvested *title phrase* with no value ever extracted, so the "produced by the pipeline" guarantee would fall from a NOT NULL FK to a registered check — and the owner's constraint is epistemic, so it belongs in DDL. It also leaves no home for the mint rationale or the element/room qualifier.
- **Coded registry `code PK, canonical_label UNIQUE`** (walkability plan §9.6 / re-put Q2, `/home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-08-27-hook-audit/WALKABILITY-PLAN.md:996-1009`). A `P-017` invites the same filing reflex as `E-08`, and a label column duplicates `terms.canonical_en`. Stability is had from an INTEGER PK plus a pointer without either.
- **Free-text `parameter_canonical` as the key** (the literal 08-26 wording). Rejected by the ruling's own counter-consideration and by A3-F11's instability point.
- **Restore `items` re-grained** (§9.6's "smallest fix"). Overtaken by R-01 and by "retired as a table name outright."

**The strongest case against this recommendation is already on the record — A3-F11, 2026-08-27: "the remedy recreates `items`."** A registry is a registry; once `judgment_parameters` holds *corridor width*, the next batch on a corridor slug finds it and files into it. Answering the five named problems: homonyms — the element noun is in the term (TERM-002 vs TERM-021) and `element_code` is NULL-forward for the rest; stability — INTEGER PK, label by pointer; two homes — no CHECK branch, no label column; the ambulant-vs-wheeled opposed demand on one parameter — that is two rows, one per identity lens, which is exactly what D-0182's multiplicity ruling permits and `idx_spec_row_identity` keys. The fifth, epistemic point survives in reduced form: **the existence of a parameter row still tells the next reader what has been found before.** That residual is the same one `terms` (88) and `slugs` (106) already carry, which the owner retained on 2026-09-01. Filing an extraction into an existing parameter is an adjudication with a NOT NULL rationale by a session holding the source — D-0173's exact act. If the owner regards even that residual as contamination, the remedy is not a different subject but a research-stage blind: keep `judgment_parameters` out of the frame pull, which D-0187 already shapes.

### 5. What would falsify it

- **The owner withdraws 08-26 under rule 0** (e.g. "the options put on 08-26 were framed from the old schema"). Then the question is genuinely open and this collapses to "put it fresh."
- **Re-accretion measured after batch 06:** any `search_executions.query_text`, `search_candidates.title` or `FRAME.md` line naming a `judgment_parameters` term or a value stated in one — `grep -c` after the batch; nonzero falsifies claim 4 in §2.
- **The grain is wrong on live rows:** after the first real extraction pass, `SELECT term_id, COUNT(*) FROM judgment_parameters WHERE status='active' GROUP BY term_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1` non-empty (the partial unique index would refuse, so the falsifier is an executing session needing two active parameters for one term with no element/room difference).
- **`terms` is the wrong vocabulary:** after batch 06, `SELECT outcome, COUNT(*) FROM parameter_adjudications GROUP BY 1` shows NAMES-NEW near 100% — the pointer buys nothing.
- **`migrate_db.py --rebuild /tmp/rebuilt.db` fails on `data_20260901183203`** after the migration — the replay analysis above was wrong.
- **`run_checks.py --all`** shows the repointed `base-parameter-vocabulary` check passing with `EXAMINED: 0` and unescalated — §5(a).

### 6. Gaps

- **Synthesis's hand-off object and the two fan-in junctions** (ruled 08-27) are undesigned; `bpc_metadata` keyed by slug is the occupant. The ≥1-synthesis requirement on a specification cannot be DDL'd and its check has no subject yet. Out of scope here, but the migration that keys `specifications` should not pretend the fan-in exists.
- **`room_code` in the identity is my choice, not a ruling.** It is there because RT60 for a learning space and for a pool are two determinations of one parameter under one lens, and `rooms` (17 rows) exists and is ruled to become `base_room_types`. The alternative is NARROWER terms. The executing session records which.
- **Whether NAMES-NEW minting is content (DG-NON).** D-0173's precedent is session work with rationale; it has not been ruled for parameters specifically.
- **The 2026-08-25 "companion RULE on the sole-writer resolution"** — the ACTION line cites it; `grep -n 'sole.writer' references/project-standards.md` did not find a RULE by that name. I carry only the ACTION: do not build `add-specification --state stated`.
- **`v_code_floor_only` / `jurisdictional_values`** is an owner question per D-0185. I give a derivation, not a disposition.
- I did not open the 21 Python and 12 skill callers; the counts are name-grep, dated today.

## ITEM 2 — Should the prior-version corpus be archived?

### 1. Recommendation

**Yes, by class and in two tranches: tranche 1 (decision-ready, low cost, mostly §8-territory) moves every file that PRESENTS the item layer as live structure — `index.html`, the Part-4 indexes, registers and matrices under `references/`, `references/audit-briefs/` (58 files named by item code), `references/connections/`, `references/conflict-matrices/`, `references/website/data/`, the five `working/` subtrees, and `versions/` — to `_archived/<same path>` with one README per directory and their orphaned skills and scripts deleted; tranche 2 (owner ruling required, real sweep cost) decides `references/bpc/**` and the analytic essays that merely cite items; and nothing already under `.ignore` by adjudication, the ledger, `references/bpc-reasoning/`, `references/search-log/`, `working/claims-docket.md` or the governance registries moves at all.**

### 2. Derivation

**Has it been ruled?** Partly, and the ruling points the way. DR-2026-08-06 §2 kept the file surfaces *"exactly as they were, as reference"* — for the *source* reset. DR-2026-08-19 §1.2 then named these same surfaces the second contamination vector for *items* and chose conduct rules (§1.4 rule 5, blind-first) over archiving. Batch 04 broke those rules (item values "22 N" and "PTV ≥36" reached agonist queries), which is why R-01 deleted the layer. **D-0186 (2026-09-02) then ruled the render half:** archive `site/`, and explicitly rejected *"treat site/ as a frozen reference surface… it keeps publishing determinations the data no longer holds."* It recorded `index.html`'s rewrite as owed and mission-level. Nobody has put `references/`, `working/` or `versions/` to the owner. So: the principle is ruled for render; the content surfaces are the owner's under §8.

**The measurement.** By directory, `grep -rEl '\b[A-K]-[0-9]{2}\b' references/ versions/ working/ index.html | awk -F/ '{print $1"/"$2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. Densest carriers (`grep -rEc`, 2026-09-09, `[A-E]`): `versions/current/…v9-0…md` 632, `versions/8.10/…md` 615, `references/claim-reference-join.json` 528, `working/mobile-app-prototype-v9/guidebook-app.jsx` 251, `references/connection-network.json` 182, `references/website/data/economics.json` 181, `references/connections/_index.md` 100, `references/part04-item-index.md` 69, `index.html` 65, `references/toc.md` 59. The E-08 name verbatim: `grep -rl 'Corridor Clear Width' references/ versions/ working/ index.html site/ parts/ tools/` → 12 files including `parts/v10/part04.md` (render, last regenerated 2026-08-12 against a then-populated `items`).

**Executable callers, because a blocking check going vacuous is DR-2026-08-06's objection to moving:** `grep -rn -E "references/(bpc|connections|…)|working/|versions/" scripts/ tools/*.py .github/workflows/ governance/check-registry.yaml`. The finding that changes DR-08-06's conclusion: `scripts/item_audit_pipeline.py` — the sole reader of `versions/current/` and the stated reason `versions/` was "unmovable" — was culled on 2026-08-20. `versions/` is now movable. `references/search-log/` is still globbed by blocking `validate_cross_refs.py` and stays. `validate_bpc.py --all` (blocking, always) prints `EXAMINED: 0` and exits 0 on an empty `references/bpc/` — `run_checks.py` escalates a blocking-and-vacuous pass, so that check must be retired in the same PR as any move of `references/bpc/`. `validate_cross_refs.py` keeps `parts/**` and `skills/**` subjects after a move of `bpc`/`connections`, so it does not go vacuous. `scripts/audit_consolidator.py` reads `references/audit-briefs/` and is **not in the check registry** — an uncalled script (§8).

**Skills are callers:** 15 files under `skills/` name the corpus paths (command in the log: `grep -rln -E 'references/(bpc|connections|toc|…)|working/|versions/|index\.html' skills/`). Most are prior-version workflow skills (`toc-editor`, `item-specification-writer`, `item-audit-pipeline`, `connection-discovery`, `audit-consolidator`…).

**Frozen citations, the cost side:** `grep -rlE '"(references|versions|working)/' attestations/ | wc -l` → 15 (7 cite `references/search-log`, 4 `references/bpc-reasoning`, 3 `references/bpc`); `grep -rlE '\b(references|versions|working)/' decisions/ | wc -l` → 41; `index.html` is cited by 9 attestations. `schemas/attestation.schema.json` types `evidence_path` as a string and no check resolves it, so nothing reddens; but rule 4 says prose callers are not covered, and the 2026-09-09 precedent (`pipeline-map.yaml` → `_archived/governance/`) accepted exactly this cost with a ledger note, relying on `_archived/` mirroring origin paths.

**What archiving does and does not buy.** `_archived/` is already hidden from ripgrep and the Grep tool; `grep -r`, `git grep`, Glob and Read still reach it, and CLAUDE.md §7 itself tells sessions to use `grep -r`. So archiving changes **what a hit says about itself** — `_archived/references/toc.md` is labelled by its path; `references/toc.md` reads as live — not whether it can be hit. That is DR-2026-08-06 §4's asymmetry argument (invisible-and-wrong fails loudly, readable-and-wrong fails confidently) and it is the whole benefit.

### 4. Alternatives rejected, and the strongest case against

- **Leave in place under §1.4 conduct rules** — tried; batch 04 broke them; that is R-01's own history.
- **Extend `.ignore`** — owner-gated on the same footing (DR-2026-08-06 §3 admission rule), search-only, and it would hide the ledger and `bpc-reasoning` unless negated; a reader who opens `references/toc.md` by name is untouched.
- **Delete** — §8 reserves `_archived/` for content; D-0186 corrected exactly this error on 09-02 (93 pages deleted, then restored to `_archived/site/specs/`).
- **Tombstone banners in place** — edits frozen records; `.ignore`'s header and §1.4 rule 4 both require the record stay as it was.
- **Archive fork (⚑1)** — blocked (403) and superseded for legibility by `.ignore`; the only option that removes `grep -r` reach; the owner's if ever.

**Strongest case against tranche 1:** DR-2026-08-19 §1.3 makes the 93 items *"a lead list, not a backup"* and §1.4 rule 1 says the list may be consulted for coverage; D-0185 restored 83 leads from `_archived/data/jurisdictional_values/` on 09-02 precisely because "~72 of the 83 leads exist nowhere else." The connection register, conflict matrices and divergence matrix are that kind of lead. Archiving does not destroy them — D-0185 proves the retrieval path works — so the objection reduces to convenience, and a coverage check reads more honestly from an archive path than from a live index. The second real cost is the 41 DRs and 15 attestations whose paths dangle in prose; the 09-09 precedent accepted it, and `_archived/` mirroring origin paths is the mitigation.

### 5. What would falsify it

- **The path still gets walked:** after tranche 1 and the next batch, `grep -cE '\b[A-K]-[0-9]{2}\b'` over that batch's `FRAME.md`, every new `search_executions.query_text` and `search_candidates.title` is nonzero — the reader reached `_archived/` or the DB rows, and the file move bought nothing.
- **A blocking check went vacuous:** `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --all` after the move reports a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE blocking check that was not retired in the same PR.
- **A caller was missed:** `git grep -l '<moved path>' -- skills scripts governance .claude tools` nonzero for any moved path after the sweep.
- **The owner reaffirms DR-08-06 §2 for `references/bpc/**`** — tranche 2 is void and the 34 code-carrying BPC files remain the largest unhidden carrier; the residual mitigation is the D-0187 research-frame blind plus directory-level READMEs.
- **`index.html` turns out to be served** (no CNAME, no Pages workflow found, but I could not check outside the repo) — then its replacement is urgent content, not archival housekeeping.

### 6. Gaps

- Classes were assigned by directory, filename and hit density plus the top-level `references/*.md` by name; I did not open all 235 files. A per-file pass is the executing session's, and some Class A/B boundaries (e.g. `references/opus-divergence-synthesis.md`) may move on reading.
- The 15 corpus-naming skills were not read to decide re-point versus delete.
- `parts/88_to_90`, `parts/deprecated` and the embedded JSON in `tools/*.html` (DR-08-19 §1.2 named the latter) were outside my sweep path; `regenerate_derived.sh` should cover `tools/`, unmeasured.
- Whether `references/slug-registry.md`, `standards-registry.md`, `search-log.md`, the `*-verified-sources.json` and `bibliography-v11-draft.md` are dual homes of DB tables is a real question I did not answer; it is not the item-code question.
- I could not determine from inside the repository whether anything external links to `index.html`.
